cohort: 104 pregnant nulliparous women in their third trimester in Semirom, Iran
finding: Positive attitudes towards NVD, supportive subjective norms, and greater perceived behavioral control were significantly associated with intention to have NVD.
mod_finding: This study, investigating factors influencing delivery mode choice, found that positive attitudes towards natural vaginal delivery (NVD), supportive social norms around NVD, and a perceived sense of control over achieving NVD significantly predicted the intention to have NVD and ultimately increased the likelihood of NVD.
